'''Neena Gupta''' (born 24 November 1984<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Dutta |first=Amartya Kumar |date=January 2025 |title=Neena Gupta: Blazing a Trail |url=https://bhavana.org.in/neena-gupta-blazing-a-trail/ |journal=Bhāvanā |volume=9 |issue=1}}</ref>) is an [[Indian people|Indian]] [[mathematician]] and professor at the Statistics and Mathematics Unit of the [[Indian Statistical Institute]] (ISI), [[Kolkata]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.isical.ac.in/faculty.php?pagemode=search&fname=neena%20gupta&fdesig=0&faddr=0&fdept=0&femail= | title=Scientific Workers | publisher=Indian Statistical Institute | access-date=15 November 2018 | archive-date=3 July 2019 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190703131704/https://www.isical.ac.in/faculty.php?pagemode=search | url-status=live }}</ref> She is known for solving [[Zariski Cancellation Problem]], originally posed by [[Oscar Zariski]] in 1949. Her primary fields of interest are [[commutative algebra]] and [[Affine variety|affine algebraic geometry]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Neena Gupta: in love with mathematics|newspaper=[[Mint (newspaper)|Mint]]|url=https://www.livemint.com/opinion/online-views/neena-gupta-in-love-with-mathematics-11640273686261.html|date=23 December 2021|first=Dilip|last=D'Souza|author-link=Dilip D'Souza}}</ref>

== Education ==
Gupta graduated with honours in mathematics from [[Bethune College]] in 2006. She earned her post graduation in mathematics from the [[Indian Statistical Institute]] in 2008<ref name="bethune">{{cite web|title=Alumnus Page|url=http://www.bethunecollege.ac.in/BethuneProud/BethuneCollege-MakeUsProud.htm|publisher=Bethune College|access-date=5 Sep 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160915221329/http://www.bethunecollege.ac.in/BethuneProud/BethuneCollege-MakeUsProud.htm|archive-date=15 September 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> and subsequently, her [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] degree in 2011 with [[commutative algebra]] as her specialization under the guidance of Amartya Kumar Dutta. The title of her dissertation was "Some results on [[Laurent polynomial]] [[fibration]]s and Quasi A*-algebras".<ref name="mathgen">{{mathgenealogy|id=162576}}</ref>

== Career ==
Gupta was a [[Shyamaprasad Mukherjee|Shyama Prasad Mukherjee]] Research Fellow at ISI Kolkata from 2008 to 2012, and, after a visiting position at [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]] (TIFR) Mumbai, became INSPIRE Faculty at ISI Kolkata in 2012.<ref name="insainspr">{{cite web|title=INSA 2012 INSPIRE Fellowships|url=http://insaindia.res.in/session2012.php|publisher=INSA|access-date=28 Aug 2016|archive-date=28 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160828234557/http://insaindia.res.in/session2012.php|url-status=dead}}</ref> She has been a professor in the Statistical and Mathematics Unit of ISI Kolkata since 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Archived copy |url=https://www.isical.ac.in/~statmath/faculty.php |access-date=21 June 2022}}</ref>

She has won the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]] (2019) in the category of mathematical sciences, the highest honor in India in the field of science and technology.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Pandey |first1=Jhimli Mukherjee |date=28 September 2019 |title=Kolkata mathematician wins Bhatnagar award, youngest recipient till date |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/kolkata/kol-mathematician-wins-bhatnagar-award-youngest-recipient-till-date/articleshow/71342310.cms |newspaper=[[The Times of India]]}}</ref> In 2022 she was awarded the [[ICTP Ramanujan Prize|ICTP Ramanujan award]]. She is the third woman from India who got this award (after the duo [[Raman Parimala]] (1987 – [[Sujatha Ramdorai]] (2004)).

Neena Gupta received the [[Indian National Science Academy]] Young Scientist award in 2014.<ref name="insa">{{cite web |date=19 September 2015 |title=Young Scientists Awards |url=http://www.insaindia.org/youngmedal.php |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20131011230428/http://www.insaindia.org/youngmedal.php |archive-date=11 October 2013 |access-date=28 Aug 2016 |publisher=INSA}}</ref> She solved the Zariski Cancellation Problem.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Gupta |first=Neena |date=2014-01-01 |title=On the cancellation problem for the affine space <math>\mathbb{A}^{3}</math> in characteristic <math>p</math> |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s00222-013-0455-2 |journal=Inventiones Mathematicae |language=en |volume=195 |issue=1 |pages=279–288 |doi=10.1007/s00222-013-0455-2 |issn=1432-1297 |url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name="barilan">{{cite web |title=On the Zariski Cancellation Problem |url=http://math.biu.ac.il/en/node/1569 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160828225754/http://math.biu.ac.il/en/node/1569 |archive-date=28 August 2016 |access-date=28 Aug 2016 |publisher=Bar-Ilan University}}</ref> Her work has also earned her the inaugural Saraswathi Cowsik Medal in 2013, awarded by the TIFR Alumni Association.<ref name="tifr">{{cite web |title=TIFR Endowment Fund Awards |url=http://www.tifr.res.in/~endowment/endowment-awards.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161229180141/http://www.tifr.res.in/~endowment/endowment-awards.htm |archive-date=29 December 2016 |access-date=28 Aug 2016 |publisher=TIFR}}</ref>
